  • InPost completes its transition to private ownership, backed by a Consortium committed to accelerating its growth as a leading European consumer-centric e-commerce enabler.
  • InPost remains operationally independent and headquartered in Poland, led by CEO and founder Rafał Brzoska and the existing management team.
  • Advent, FedEx, A&R and PPF bring together long-term capital, deep sector knowledge, complementary commercial expertise and broad industry networks to help drive InPost’s future growth across Europe.
  • The Consortium will accelerate investment in InPost’s pan-European out-of-home network, underpinned by continued innovation in its technology platform and consumer proposition.
  • InPost’s growth strategy will be supported by arm’s length commercial agreements connecting InPost’s B2C last-mile capabilities to FedEx’s global network of c.3 million businesses and 225 million recipients.
  • The transaction will seek to deliver tangible benefits across InPost’s growing network, from stronger delivery infrastructure for merchants and greater convenience for consumers across Poland and Western Europe to continued career growth opportunities for employees.

AMSTERDAM & LUXEMBOURG--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Funds managed and/or advised by Advent International, L.P. and/or its affiliates (“Advent”), FCWB LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of FedEx Corporation (“FedEx”), A&R Investments Ltd. (“A&R”) and PPF Group (“PPF”), together forming the Consortium, today announce the completion of the acquisition of InPost S.A. (“InPost” or the “Company”). InPost is now wholly-owned by the Consortium and has delisted from Euronext Amsterdam.

A new chapter for InPost

Completion of the acquisition marks a significant milestone for InPost, a leading European out-of-home e-commerce enablement platform. The business will continue to operate as a standalone, operationally independent company under its existing brand, with its headquarters, management structure and innovation remaining in Poland. Founder Rafał Brzoska continues to lead the Company as CEO, and the executive leadership team which has underpinned InPost’s success to date remains in place, carrying forward the vision he set out when founding the business in 1999.

With an out-of-home network of over 100,000 locations, comprising more than 70,000 automated parcel lockers and close to 30,000 pick-up and drop-off points, the Consortium believes InPost has a clear path to extend its reach further. Backed by the Consortium’s capital, expertise, deep sector experience and shared vision, InPost will work to strengthen its position in Poland and expand across Europe, including in the UK, Italy, France, Spain, Portugal and the Benelux region. InPost’s home market of Poland will remain the blueprint for new innovations, which will then be scaled across InPost’s wider European network.

At its core, InPost is a technology-driven business aiming to redefine the European e-commerce sector by improving the delivery experience for consumers and merchants alike. The Consortium will accelerate investment in InPost’s digital offering and consumer experience, including its mobile app, as it innovates to increase its consumer appeal. Enabled by this technology platform and leading out-of-home network, the Consortium believes InPost is well-positioned to benefit from structural sector tailwinds, including increasing e-commerce penetration, rising consumer demand for speed and convenience, and the shift towards more sustainable delivery solutions.

To help deliver this growth, InPost and FedEx are exploring separate commercial opportunities to provide FedEx merchants access to InPost’s B2C capabilities while leveraging FedEx’s global network to support the Company’s growth. As an example, the two companies have entered into arm’s length commercial agreements enabling selected recipients the use of InPost’s last-mile capabilities and out-of-home infrastructure in Europe.

The partnership between the Consortium and InPost aims to deliver benefits for all InPost stakeholders. Employees will continue to be able to build their careers within a strengthened business, empowered by a fast-growing, innovative culture. Merchants can expect a more advanced, better-connected delivery network and continued investment in the technology that serves their consumers. And consumers across Poland and Western Europe will have the opportunity to experience greater convenience, more choice and a faster way to shop and receive goods – driven by InPost’s consumer-centric innovations and growing delivery network.

The Consortium believes its investment, collective sector knowledge and experience will support InPost in continuing to build a leading platform for parcel delivery and returns across Europe.

Rafał Brzoska, Founder and CEO of InPost, said: “This partnership delivers the long-term capital, global reach and deep technology expertise we require to build on what we have already achieved together as a leading European e-commerce enabler. I’m proud of how far we have come since founding InPost in 1999 in Poland, growing into one of Europe’s largest delivery networks. We’re taking this step with partners who have known InPost for years and understand our business and ambitions. With the Consortium’s expertise and backing, we will accelerate our investment in the technology and consumer experience that set us apart, bringing them to even more consumers and merchants across Europe.”

Ranjan Sen, Managing Partner at Advent, said: “We began our journey with InPost and Rafał in 2017, when we invested in a promising local leader with the potential to become a European champion. InPost has since grown to over 100,000 locations across Poland and Western Europe, and we are proud to reiterate our conviction in Rafał and his team. Drawing on our successful track record of investing in both InPost and the wider logistics sector, we look forward to working alongside our Consortium partners to help drive the next stage of the Company’s growth.”

Raj Subramaniam, President and CEO of FedEx, said: “FedEx is the heartbeat of the global industrial economy, and InPost has built a leading position in Europe’s out-of-home delivery segment. Connecting our global network of 3 million businesses and 225 million recipients with InPost’s last-mile capabilities gives both businesses a potential springboard for profitable growth. We see significant opportunity to expand our commercial arrangements across Europe and look forward to building on it as members of the Consortium.”

Didier Stoessel, Co-CEO of PPF, said: “When we first invested in InPost almost three years ago, we saw a strong business model with long-term growth potential as e-commerce and out-of-home delivery continue to expand across Europe. Our conviction in the Company has only strengthened since then. We are pleased to build on that relationship now by reinvesting alongside our Consortium partners and leveraging our knowledge of the Company as InPost enters this next chapter.”

Consortium structure

Following completion, the Consortium is structured with Advent holding 37%, FedEx holding 37%, A&R holding 16% and PPF holding 10%. A&R has fully rolled-over its holdings in the Company and PPF has reinvested part of the proceeds from the tender of its existing stake to become a shareholder in the Consortium.

Notes to Editors:

About InPost

InPost has revolutionised e-commerce parcel delivery in Poland and is now one of the leading out-of-home e-commerce enablement platforms in Europe. Founded in 1999 by Rafał Brzoska, InPost provides delivery services through our network of more than 70,000 Automated Parcel Machines (“APMs”) across nine European countries, alongside courier and fulfilment services for e-commerce merchants. InPost’s locker network provides consumers with a cheaper, more flexible and convenient delivery option. Powered by in-house technology, InPost continuously develops and tests new services, from digital tools to e-commerce solutions, to make buying and selling online simpler for consumers and merchants.

About Advent

Advent is a leading global private equity investor committed to working in partnership with management teams, entrepreneurs, and founders to help transform businesses. With 17 offices across five continents, we oversee more than USD $109 billion in assets under management* and have made 460 investments across 45 countries.

Since our founding in 1984, we have developed specialist market expertise across our five core sectors: business & financial services, consumer, healthcare, industrial, and technology. This approach is bolstered by our deep sub-sector knowledge, which informs every aspect of our investment strategy, from sourcing opportunities to working in partnership with management to execute value creation plans. We bring hands-on operational expertise to enhance and accelerate businesses.

As one of the largest privately-owned partnerships, our 675 colleagues leverage the full ecosystem of Advent’s global resources, including our Portfolio Support Group, insights provided by industry expert Operating Partners and Operations Advisors, as well as bespoke tools to support and guide our portfolio companies as they seek to achieve their strategic goals.

*Assets under management (AUM) as of June 30, 2026. AUM includes assets attributable to Advent advisory clients as well as employee and third-party co-investment vehicles.

About FedEx

FedEx Corp. (NYSE: FDX) provides customers and businesses worldwide with a broad portfolio of transportation, ecommerce, and business services. With annual revenue of $86 billion, the company offers integrated business solutions utilizing its flexible, efficient, and intelligent global network. Consistently ranked among the world’s most admired and trusted employers, FedEx inspires its more than 450,000 employees to remain focused on safety, the highest ethical and professional standards, and the needs of their customers and communities. FedEx is committed to connecting people and possibilities around the world responsibly and resourcefully, with a goal to achieve carbon-neutral operations by 2040. To learn more, please visit fedex.com/about.

About A&R

A&R is an independent investment company founded by Rafał Brzoska that manages a diversified portfolio of private and public investments. A&R has been a shareholder in InPost since its IPO.

About PPF

PPF Group, a privately held investment holding company, operates in 25 countries across Europe, North America and Asia. It invests in telecommunications, media, financial services, real estate, ecommerce, industry, biotechnology and other sectors. PPF Group held assets worth EUR 42.1 billion and employed approximately 34,000 people worldwide (as of 30 June 2026).

HUNTINGTON BEACH, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Karman Space & Defense (NYSE: KRMN) has been awarded a five-year, $31 million contract by the Naval Surface Warfare Center, Carderock Division, to produce propulsor tailcones for the U.S. Navy’s Virginia-class attack submarines.

Virginia-class fast-attack submarine USS Colorado (SSN 788) returns from sea trials at Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam on June 6, 2026.

The award helps the Navy secure long-lead materials, reduce production risk, and strengthen the submarine industrial base.

“The Navy’s ability to expand submarine production depends on a reliable industrial base capable of delivering highly specialized capabilities at scale,” said Jon Rambeau, chief executive officer of Karman Space & Defense. “Meeting that challenge requires sustained investment in advanced manufacturing capabilities and a relentless focus on execution.”

The contract is structured primarily as firm-fixed-price, with cost-plus-fixed-fee options for nonrecurring engineering and specialized engineering services supporting manufacturing strategy development and production implementation.

The award builds on Karman’s longstanding involvement in submarine programs, expanding the company’s content on Virginia-class submarines and reinforcing its role in supporting the Navy’s production requirements.

Karman’s Gulfport, Mississippi, operations bring decades of deep engineering and manufacturing experience to the nation’s submarine programs. The team produces composite structures and propulsion-related components designed to meet the demanding performance and reliability requirements of undersea missions.

Karman Space & Defense is the specialized engineering and manufacturing partner behind many of the nation’s most critical space and defense programs. Key Terms

firm-fixed-pricefinancial
A firm-fixed-price contract sets a single, unchanging price for goods or services that the seller must deliver, regardless of how much those costs rise or fall during performance. For investors, this matters because the buyer bears little cost uncertainty while the seller absorbs any cost overruns, which can make revenue more predictable but can squeeze profit margins if expenses increase—think of agreeing to buy a product at a set price even if the seller’s costs go up.
cost-plus-fixed-feefinancial
Cost-plus-fixed-fee is a payment method used in contracting where the buyer agrees to cover all the costs of a project plus an additional fixed amount as profit. This means the total payment depends on the actual expenses incurred, plus a set fee that doesn’t change regardless of the project's final costs. For investors, understanding this arrangement helps assess how project costs and profit margins are managed and how they might impact financial risk and potential returns.

  • Commercialization partnership with Amarox provides fully funded in-country distribution and a 50/50 revenue share while building localized biopharma capabilities
  • Saudi FDA’s New Accelerator Program for Drugs in Rare Diseases (NADR) grants priority access and scientific flexibility, advancing Saudi Vision 2030 healthcare initiatives

VIENNA, Va.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- CEL-SCI Corporation (NYSE American: CVM) today announced that its investigational cancer immunotherapy Multikine® (Leukocyte Interleukin, Injection) has been granted official designation under the Saudi Food and Drug Authority’s (SFDA) New Accelerator Program for Drugs in Rare Diseases (NADR). The designation application was successfully submitted by Amarox, CEL-SCI’s in-country regulatory and commercialization partner in Saudi Arabia.

The NADR designation positions Saudi Arabia to potentially become the first commercial market globally for Multikine®. With NADR status secured, CEL-SCI and Amarox are preparing to submit a Marketing Authorization Application (MAA) to the SFDA within the next 2-3 months. Under recently enacted SFDA guidance, products designated under the NADR pathway qualify for priority review with a target assessment timeframe of 160 working days, supporting a potential commercial launch and initial commercial sales of Multikine in 2027 or early 2028, pending SFDA approval and review of the MAA.

“The Saudi FDA has demonstrated extraordinary global regulatory leadership by establishing the NADR program,” stated Geert Kersten, Chief Executive Officer of CEL-SCI. “Their forward-looking framework perfectly aligns with Saudi Vision 2030’s mandate to bring cutting-edge healthcare innovations to the Kingdom rapidly. Because of the SFDA's proactive approach, we are prioritizing Saudi Arabia as the potential first global commercial market for Multikine. Supported by Amarox’s deep in-country capabilities, we are not only advancing our commercialization strategy but also supporting the Kingdom’s goal of building robust, localized biopharmaceutical infrastructure. This partnership de-risks our commercial transition while delivering on our shared commitment to urgently bring life-extending therapies to head and neck cancer patients. Multikine® will initially be supplied from CEL-SCI’s US based manufacturing facility.”

“Our partnership with CEL-SCI represents an important step in Saudi Amarox’s strategy to expand into innovative medicines, advanced therapies, and biotechnology,” said Dr. Abdullah Alzomaie, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Saudi Amarox. “We are proud of CEL-SCI’s confidence in Amarox as its regional partner, and we are pleased to see our collaboration achieve an important early milestone through the SFDA’s NADR designation for Multikine. This progress reflects the encouraging environment Saudi Arabia is creating under Vision 2030 to support medical innovation, scientific research, and the introduction of advanced therapies. We see this as the beginning of a promising and long-term partnership.”

Accelerated Regulatory Pathway Aligned with Saudi Vision 2030

Launched by the SFDA in August 2026, the NADR program is a cornerstone initiative supporting the healthcare transformation goals of Saudi Vision 2030 and the Kingdom's National Biotechnology Strategy. NADR is designed to expedite the evaluation of breakthrough therapies that address serious diseases with high unmet medical needs, ensuring Saudi citizens have first-in-class access to advanced medicines. Key benefits of the designation include:

  • Priority 160-Working-Day Assessment: Eligibility for accelerated review under SFDA submission guidance effective January 1, 2027, establishing a clear pathway for a potential 2027 or early 2028 Multikine launch.
  • Collaborative Regulatory Framework: Dedicated access to scientific advice and tailored evaluation frameworks, reflecting the SFDA's commitment to agile, science-based regulation.
  • Streamlined Access Pathways: Accelerated frameworks designed to bring high-impact immunotherapies to patients rapidly.

Capital-Efficient Commercialization & Local Capability Building

Under the terms of the strategic partnership announced in May 2026, Amarox is CEL-SCI’s local regulatory representative and exclusive commercial distributor for Multikine in Saudi Arabia. Beyond establishing a capital-efficient, 50% / 50% net revenue-sharing model for CEL-SCI, the partnership directly supports Saudi Arabia's localization goals by utilizing fully funded, in-country marketing, logistics, and sales infrastructure. The agreement also includes an option to expand this localized commercial framework into the broader Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) member states—including the United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, and Oman.

Compelling Phase 3 Clinical Foundation

CEL-SCI intends to seek marketing authorization in Saudi Arabia for the exact target population defined in its planned U.S. registration study: newly diagnosed, previously untreated adult patients with locally advanced, resectable oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma with no lymph node involvement and low/zero tumor PD-L1 expression.

In the world’s largest Phase 3 study for locally advanced head and neck cancer, neoadjuvant treatment with Multikine® before standard of care (SOC) delivered dramatic survival benefits in this target population:

  • 73% 5-Year Overall Survival vs. 45% for SOC alone (p = 0.0015).
  • 66% Relative Reduction in Risk of Death compared to SOC alone (Hazard Ratio = 0.34).
  • Strong Neoadjuvant Mechanism: Administered locally over three weeks immediately following diagnosis, activating an intact immune system prior to surgery, radiation, and chemotherapy.

First Berlin, based in Berlin, Germany, which facilitated the partnership, continues to support CEL-SCI and Amarox as the program moves towards submission and launch in the Kingdom.

About Multikine

Multikine is a novel cancer immunotherapy administered before surgery as a treatment for newly diagnosed previously untreated locally advanced head and neck cancer. It is manufactured at scale, stored in a vial, and injected directly around the tumor. Its goal is to activate a person’s immune system to fight cancer before the ravages of surgery, radiation and chemotherapy have weakened the immune system. In the world’s largest locally advanced head and neck cancer Phase 3 study, Multikine increased the 5-year survival rate of the target patient population to 73% vs 45% in patients treated with standard of care alone and halved the risk of death from 55% to 27%.

About CEL-SCI Corporation

CEL-SCI believes that boosting a patient’s immune system before surgery, radiotherapy and chemotherapy have damaged it, should provide the greatest possible impact on survival. Multikine is designed to help the immune system "target" the tumor at a time when the immune system is still relatively intact and thereby thought to be better able to mount an attack on the tumor.

Multikine (Leukocyte Interleukin, Injection), given right after diagnosis and before surgery, has been administered to over 740 patients and has an excellent safety profile compared to other cancer drugs. It has received Orphan Drug designation from the FDA for neoadjuvant therapy in patients with squamous cell carcinoma (cancer) of the head and neck.

The Company has operations in Vienna, Virginia, and near/in Baltimore, Maryland.

Key Terms

marketing authorization applicationregulatory
A marketing authorization application is a formal request submitted to a government regulator asking permission to sell a prescription medicine or medical product in a country or region. Think of it like asking for a business license after showing evidence the product is safe and works; investors care because approval determines whether the product can generate sales, how soon revenue starts, and how much regulatory risk and uncertainty remains.
hazard ratiomedical
A hazard ratio is a way scientists compare the chance of something happening over time between two groups, like patients taking different medicines. If the ratio is high, it means one group is more likely to experience the event sooner or more often, which helps determine how effective a treatment is or how risky a situation might be.
neoadjuvantmedical
"Neoadjuvant" describes treatments or interventions that are given before the main or primary procedure, such as surgery or a major decision. It’s like preparing the ground before planting seeds, aiming to improve the final outcome. For investors, understanding neoadjuvant approaches can provide insight into how companies enhance results or effectiveness in their processes or products.
pd-l1medical
PD-L1 is a protein found on the surface of some cells that acts like a stop sign for the immune system, telling certain immune cells to back off. It matters to investors because many cancer drugs and diagnostic tests target or measure PD-L1 to unlock immune responses or predict which patients will benefit, affecting clinical success, regulatory approval, and potential sales in the oncology market.

KUALA LUMPUR, MY / ACCESS Newswire / November 20, 2026 / AsiaFIN Holdings Corp. (OTCQB:ASFH), a global financial ecosystem enabler, today announced the appointment of Fortune Angel INC, a New York corporation based in Manhattan, New York, as its non-exclusive U.S. reseller partner for the marketing, sales, training and customer support of OrangeFIN Asia's flagship Agentic and Robotic Process Automation ("APA-RPA") Software-as-a-Service ("SaaS") solution, OrangeWorkforce. OrangeFIN is a wholly owned subsidiary of AsiaFIN Holdings Corp.

The partnership represents an important milestone in AsiaFIN's international expansion strategy, establishing an initial commercial presence in New York and the East Coast of the United States. Through this collaboration, AsiaFIN aims to introduce its established automation platform to U.S. businesses, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises ("SMEs") seeking to improve operational efficiency, streamline business processes and accelerate digital transformation.

OrangeFIN's APA-RPA SaaS platform has been deployed across more than 100 client organizations in Asia and the Middle East, supporting businesses across a broad range of industry verticals, including banking and financial services, logistics, oil and gas, wholesale and distribution, property management, education, legal services, healthcare, food and beverage, agriculture and manufacturing.

OrangeWorkforce combines agentic automation capabilities with robotic process automation to help organizations automate repetitive and complex workflows, improve productivity, reduce manual processing and enhance operational efficiency.

Building on its established regional customer base and implementation experience, AsiaFIN sees the U.S. market as an important opportunity to expand its recurring SaaS revenue streams and scale its technology business internationally.

Commercial Partnership and Responsibilities

Under the non-exclusive reseller arrangement, OrangeFIN has granted Fortune Angel INC the rights to market and resell OrangeWorkforce APA-RPA software products in object-code form within the agreed commercial scope.

The reseller's responsibilities include:

  • Marketing and Sales: Promoting and reselling AsiaFIN's designated APA-RPA software solutions to prospective U.S. customers.
  • Customer Training: Supporting customer onboarding, product familiarization and training activities using OrangeFIN's approved software materials.
  • Customer Support: Providing first-level and second-level technical and customer support for the APA-RPA software.
  • Market Development: Identifying potential customers and developing commercial opportunities across SMEs and other business sectors in the United States.

The partnership will initially focus on New York and the East Coast, with the potential to explore additional U.S. markets as commercial opportunities develop.

Mr. KC Wong, Chief Executive Officer of AsiaFIN Holdings Corp., said, "We are pleased to appoint Fortune Angel INC as our U.S. reseller partner as we take an important step towards expanding OrangeFIN's APA-RPA business into the American market.

We believe this experience provides a strong foundation for introducing our automation capabilities to U.S. businesses, particularly SMEs looking to enhance productivity, streamline operations and embrace the next generation of intelligent automation.

"Through Fortune Angel's local market presence and customer engagement capabilities, we aim to establish a scalable sales, training and support channel, beginning in New York and the East Coast. This partnership is also aligned with our broader strategy of growing our technology and recurring SaaS businesses beyond our established markets.

"We see significant opportunities in the convergence of agentic AI and robotic process automation, and remain committed to developing and delivering innovative solutions that create sustainable long-term value for our customers and shareholders," Mr. Wong concluded.

Ms. Qi Feng, Chief Executive Officer of Fortune Angel INC, said, "We are delighted to partner with AsiaFIN to introduce its APA-RPA solutions to SME business communities in New York City and the East Coast.

"AsiaFIN's established automation platform, supported by deployments across more than 100 client organizations in the world and a broad range of industry verticals, presents an exciting opportunity for American businesses seeking practical and scalable automation solutions.

"We look forward to leveraging our local business networks, sales capabilities and customer support resources to bring these solutions to SMEs and other businesses. Our goal is to help organizations automate complex processes, improve operational efficiency and unlock new opportunities for growth through intelligent automation.

"We believe this partnership provides a strong platform for introducing world-class agentic and robotic automation capabilities to the U.S. business community."

Key Terms

greenhouse gas (ghg)technical
Gases such as carbon dioxide and methane that trap heat in the atmosphere, like a blanket around the planet. For investors they matter because regulation, consumer demand and physical climate impacts driven by these gases can change costs, asset values and long-term profitability; companies that reduce emissions may face lower regulatory risk and attract capital, while high emitters can face fines, higher operating costs or stranded assets.
scope 1 and scope 2technical
Scope 1 emissions are the greenhouse gases a company directly produces from sources it owns or controls, like fuel burned in company vehicles or on-site boilers. Scope 2 emissions are the indirect greenhouse gases associated with the electricity, heat or steam the company buys and uses. Investors use these measures like a household checking its own gas usage versus its electricity bill: they reveal a company’s operational carbon footprint, exposure to energy costs and regulatory or reputational risks.
scope 3technical
Scope 3 describes all greenhouse gas emissions that occur upstream and downstream of a company’s direct operations—things like emissions from suppliers, transportation, product use, and disposal. Think of it as the hidden carbon footprint tied to everything a business buys, sells, or enables; it matters to investors because these indirect emissions can drive regulatory costs, supply-chain disruption, consumer preference shifts, and long-term valuation risk that aren’t visible on a company’s factory floor or utility bill.
sasbregulatory
SASB stands for the Sustainability Accounting Standards Board, an organization that created industry-specific guidelines for companies to report environmental, social and governance factors that are likely to affect their financial performance. Think of it as a standardized checklist that helps investors compare how well different companies manage risks like pollution, labor practices or product safety — similar to using a common recipe so you can fairly judge different cooks. Clear, consistent SASB disclosures make it easier for investors to spot hidden risks and long-term value drivers.
tcfdregulatory
A framework that guides companies on reporting how climate change and related policies, physical impacts, and market shifts affect their finances and business plans. It matters to investors because consistent, comparable disclosures act like a weather forecast for financial risk—helping assess which companies face greater climate-related danger or opportunity, improving decisions about value, risk allocation, and long-term planning.

The engine is also re-tuned for quieter acceleration at low and mid-speeds. Overall output climbs to 251 total system horsepower (previously 245 horsepower) while also squeezing more miles out of every tank, with the manufacturer estimated city fuel economy rating improving by three miles per gallon (MPG) on FWD-equipped models and four MPG on AWD-equipped models to 39/35/37 (city/highway/combined) MPG on both drivetrains.

The updates to the hybrid system are complimented by handling improvements from new Electronic Power Steering components, including a new steering wheel and column, and a new Electronic Control Braking system that is intended to maximize brake feel while also minimizing body roll.

Sienna's driver and interior tech are also updated thanks to a new electrical platform. The new platform enables the latest version of Toyota Safety Sense 4.0 (TSS 4.0), making it one of the earlier Toyota models to adopt the safety system -- following the 2026 RAV4 and 2027 Tundra and Sequoia models. The new system has upgraded sensors and hardware for improved detection capabilities. The Sienna also adds a standard drive recorder dash cam.

Information and entertainment are also updated. All grades now have a 12.3-inch touchscreen powered by the latest version of Toyota's Audio Multimedia system, standard (LE grade was previously 8-inch display). For Woodland, XSE, and Platinum models equipped with the optional rear seat entertainment center, the screen size increases to 12.9-inches, up from 11.6-inches, and adopts touch screen technology.

Assembled in the U.S. in Princeton, Indiana, the 2027 Sienna is expected to arrive at Toyota dealerships across the United States by early 2027. Full line pricing will be announced at a later date.

What's New
Overall, the 2027 Sienna receives updates focused on adding comfort, confidence, and a more technologically advanced experience. New features for all grades (unless otherwise noted) include:

  • Update to Toyota Safety Sense 4.0
  • Update to latest generation of Toyota Audio Multimedia

New electric motors that use highly efficient silicon carbide conductors are also equipped, adding power with more electric assist during driving.

THS 6 is engineered for larger vehicles that need higher-capacity hybrid hardware. It uses a 124-kW drive motor, a 40-kW rear motor on AWD-equipped models, a 1.15 kWh Lithium-Ion battery, and a gear set that is engineered to handle increased weight and reaction torque. The inverter is integrated into the hybrid transaxle, which makes the system more compact, lowers the center of gravity, and reduces overall unit weight. The system also aims to reduce friction and maximize output with a new lower-viscosity e-transaxle fluid and 0W-8 engine oil.

Total system output climbs to 251 total system horsepower (previously 245 hp); engine torque remains the same at 176 lb.-ft. The Sienna can go from 0 to 60 MPH in a 7.5-seconds on the FWD model and 7.6-seconds on the AWD model (manufacturer estimated), improving from 7.9-seconds for the prior year model.

The 2027 Sienna's handling dynamics take a turn for more direct steering feel with a new steering system and software refinements. A new steering column, steering gear box, motor control unit (MCU), and torque sensor are now equipped. The system was also re-tuned to minimize steering effort at low speeds for easier parking, while increasing on-center definition for improved stability at highway speeds.

A new Electronically Controlled Brake System also comes to Sienna. This system, which debuted on the 2026 RAV4, has a master cylinder configuration with on-demand pressurization that is intended to give it optimal brake feeling and response. It also has Vehicle Braking Posture Control (VBPC) that uses braking inputs at select wheels that aim to slow the rate of body roll when turning into a corner.

The 2027 Sienna is built on the Toyota Next Generation-K (TNG-K) platform, which is engineered to resist noise intrusion and vibration through the steering, floor and vehicle structure. It has extensive, strategically placed noise insulation and body sealant intended to keep outside noises where they belong – outside.   • TREMFYA showed statistically significant improvement in disease activity on the BASDAI score versus placebo, reflecting meaningful reductions in pain, stiffness, swelling and fatigue in a Phase 4 study
  • TREMFYA demonstrated more than 2 times greater reduction in MRI-assessed inflammation versus placebo at Week 24 in the sacroiliac joints, which connect the lower spine to the pelvis and are responsible for pain and stiffness
  • TREMFYA was evaluated in first-ever PsA study using objective MRI assessments to confirm and measure axial inflammation alongside patient-reported symptoms

NEW BRUNSWICK, N.J., Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Johnson & Johnson (NYSE:JNJ) today announced late-breaking results from the Phase 4 STAR study of TREMFYA (guselkumab) in biologic-naïve adults with active psoriatic arthritis and axial involvement (axial PsA). TREMFYA met primary and major secondary endpoints that demonstrated significant improvement in axial symptoms compared to placebo and significant reduction of MRI-assessed inflammation in the sacroiliac joints.1,a The Phase 4 STAR study is the first and only dedicated randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study designed to prospectively evaluate an IL-23 inhibitor specifically in patients with axial involvement in PsA confirmed by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The late-breaking results are being presented at the Emirates Society for Rheumatology (ESR) Annual Meeting.

For people living with psoriatic arthritis, axial involvement can add another layer of burden to an already complex disease. Chronic inflammation of the spine and sacroiliac joints can cause back pain and stiffness, limiting patients' mobility and physical function.2 Axial involvement may affect approximately 5 to 28 percent of patients with early PsA and 25 to 70 percent of those with longer-standing disease.13 Despite advances in treatment, axial PsA remains challenging to classify, and very few prospective clinical trials have been dedicated specifically to this patient population, underscoring the urgent need for more robust evidence in this subset of PsA patients.

"Axial involvement in psoriatic arthritis can be difficult to identify and evaluate, leaving clinicians with limited evidence to guide patient selection for clinical trials and possibly treatment decisions," said Prof. Mikkel Ostergaard, M.D., Ph.D., DMSc, Clinical Professor of Rheumatology at the University of Copenhagen and Consultant in Rheumatology and Chairperson of the Copenhagen Center for Arthritis Research (COPECARE) at the Center for Rheumatology and Spine Diseases, Rigshospitalet, Glostrup.f "In the STAR study, TREMFYA showed significant improvements in patient-reported symptoms and MRI-assessed axial inflammation in the sacroiliac joints, backed by a well-characterized safety profile. Together, these findings provide important evidence to help inform treatment decisions for this debilitating and understudied manifestation of psoriatic arthritis."

TREMFYA demonstrated clinically meaningful improvements, reflecting reductions across patient-reported domains including spinal pain, stiffness, fatigue, joint symptoms and areas of tenderness. At Week 24, mean Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Index (BASDAI)b scores, which are on a 10-point scale, improved by −3.3 with TREMFYA 100 mg every four weeks (Q4W) and −2.9 with TREMFYA every eight weeks (Q8W) versus −2.1 with placebo.1,c

TREMFYA Q4Wc and Q8W also demonstrated significant improvements in symptoms, as measured by the Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Score using C-reactive protein (ASDAS-CRP)d compared with placebo at Week 24 (−1.5 and −1.3, respectively, versus −0.8).1 These exceeded the internationally recognized standard of ≥1.1 units for clinically important improvement, reflecting a reduction in C-reactive protein, a marker of inflammation in the body.3

TREMFYA also provided high levels of skin clearance in patients treated with TREMFYA Q4W and Q8W, consistent with skin clearance demonstrated in other PsA studies such as DISCOVER I and II and APEX.4 5 6 Additionally, the overall safety profile observed in the STAR study was consistent with the established safety profile of TREMFYA in psoriatic disease, and no new safety signals were identified.1

The notable measure in this study was MRI-assessed sacroiliac joint inflammation, measured using the Spondyloarthritis Research Consortium of Canada (SPARCC)e score. TREMFYA reduced scores by −7.1 and −5.2, with Q4W and Q8W, respectively, versus −2.4 with placebo, representing more than 2 times greater improvement than placebo.1

"Psoriatic arthritis is a complex disease that can affect patients in many ways, from skin and peripheral joint symptoms to irreversible joint damage to axial involvement," said David M. Lee, M.D., Ph.D., Global Immunology Therapeutic Area Head, Johnson & Johnson. "The STAR study brings new insight to axial PsA research showing that TREMFYA can improve axial symptoms and MRI-detected inflammation, while uniquely establishing evidence for an IL-23 inhibitor. Johnson & Johnson continues to pioneer new studies to challenge norms for patients, and these results further reinforce the role of TREMFYA in addressing the diverse manifestations of psoriatic arthritis."

Editor's notes:

a. The change from baseline in Health Assessment Questionnaire - Disability Index (HAQ-DI) was numerically greater for Q8W dosing but did not achieve statistical significance.
b. BASDAI is a validated patient-reported outcome (PRO) originally developed to measure disease activity on a 0 to 10 scale in ankylosing spondylitis (AS), now referred to as radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (r-axSpA).7
c. TREMFYA is not approved for Q4W dosing in the U.S.
d. ASDAS-CRP, or Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Score with C-Reactive Protein, is a validated, composite index that combines patient-reported symptoms with a laboratory biomarker to objectively measure inflammation and disease severity.8 9
e. The Spondyloarthritis Research Consortium of Canada (SPARCC) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) score is a validated, objective, semiquantitative scoring system used to measure active inflammatory changes in the spine and sacroiliac joint.10
f. Prof. Ostergaard is a paid consultant for Johnson & Johnson. He has not been compensated for any media work.

About the STAR study (NCT04929210)

STAR is a Phase 4, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study evaluating TREMFYA in biologic-naïve adults with active psoriatic arthritis and axial disease. Eligible participants had active PsA with objective evidence of axial inflammation confirmed by centrally read MRI and elevated C-reactive protein despite previous treatment with non-biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs), apremilast and/or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs).11

The study enrolled 411 participants worldwide and includes a 24-week placebo-controlled treatment period followed by a 24-week active treatment period. The primary endpoint evaluated change from baseline in the Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Index (BASDAI) at Week 24. Secondary endpoints include additional assessments of axial disease activity, MRI inflammation, physical function, peripheral musculoskeletal manifestations, skin disease and safety.11

About psoriatic arthritis with axial involvement

Psoriatic arthritis with axial involvement (axial PsA) is a chronic inflammatory condition where psoriatic arthritis affects the spine and sacroiliac joints (connecting the lower spine to the pelvis). It can cause inflammatory back pain, neck stiffness, and reduced mobility, in addition to the joint, skin or nail manifestations commonly associated with PsA.12 13

Despite significant advances in the treatment of psoriatic arthritis, axial involvement remains an area of substantial ongoing need and research.14 While it shares some clinical features with axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA), axial involvement is increasingly recognized as a distinct domain of psoriatic arthritis.15 However, there is currently no universally accepted definition or validated classification criteria specific to PsA with axial involvement, and prospective studies conducted exclusively in patients with axial involvement remain very limited.16

About TREMFYA (guselkumab)

Developed by Johnson & Johnson, TREMFYA is the first approved fully-human, dual-acting monoclonal antibody designed to neutralize inflammation at the cellular source by blocking IL-23 and binding to CD64 (a receptor on cells that produce IL-23). Findings for dual-acting are limited to in vitro studies that demonstrate guselkumab binds to CD64, which is expressed on the surface of IL-23 producing cells in an inflammatory monocyte model. The clinical significance of this finding is not known.

TREMFYA is a prescription medicine approved in the U.S. to treat:

  • adults and children six years and older who also weigh at least 40 kg with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis who may benefit from taking injections or pills (systemic therapy) or phototherapy (treatment using ultraviolet or UV light).
  • adults and children six years and older who also weigh at least 40 kg with active psoriatic arthritis.
  • adults with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis.
  • adults with moderately to severely active Crohn's disease.

TREMFYA is approved in Europe, Canada, Japan, and a number of other countries for the treatment of adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis, adults with active psoriatic arthritis, adults with moderate-to-severe Crohn's disease and adults with moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis.

The manufacturer for TREMFYA is Janssen Biotech, Inc.

Johnson & Johnson maintains exclusive worldwide marketing rights to TREMFYA. For more information, visit: www.tremfya.com.

IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION

What is the most important information I should know about TREMFYA?

TREMFYA is a prescription medicine that may cause serious side effects, including:

  • Serious Allergic Reactions. Stop using TREMFYA and get emergency medical help right away if you develop any of the following symptoms of a serious allergic reaction:

o fainting, dizziness, feeling lightheaded (low blood pressure)

o swelling of your face, eyelids, lips, mouth, tongue or throat

o trouble breathing or throat tightness

o chest tightness

o skin rash, hives

o itching

  • Infections. TREMFYA may lower the ability of your immune system to fight infections and may increase your risk of infections. Your healthcare provider should check you for infections and tuberculosis (TB) before starting treatment with TREMFYA and may treat you for TB before you begin treatment with TREMFYA if you have a history of TB or have active TB. Your healthcare provider should watch you closely for signs and symptoms of TB during and after treatment with TREMFYA.

Tell your healthcare provider right away if you have an infection or have symptoms of an infection, including:

o fever, sweats, or chills

o muscle aches

o weight loss

o cough

o warm, red, or painful skin or sores on your body different from your psoriasis

o diarrhea or stomach pain

o shortness of breath

o blood in your phlegm (mucus)

o burning when you urinate or urinating more often than normal

  • Liver problems. With the treatment of Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis, your healthcare provider will do blood tests to check your liver before and during treatment with TREMFYA. With the treatment of plaque psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis, your healthcare provider may do blood tests to check your liver before and as necessary during treatment with TREMFYA. Your healthcare provider may stop treatment with TREMFYA if you develop liver problems. Tell your healthcare provider right away if you notice any of the following symptoms:

o unexplained rash

o vomiting

o tiredness (fatigue)

o yellowing of the skin or the whites of your eyes

o nausea

o stomach pain (abdominal)

o loss of appetite

o dark urine

Do not use TREMFYA if you have had a serious allergic reaction to guselkumab or any of the ingredients in TREMFYA.

Before using TREMFYA, tell your healthcare provider about all of your medical conditions, including if you:

  • have any of the conditions or symptoms listed in the section "What is the most important information I should know about TREMFYA?"
  • have an infection that does not go away or that keeps coming back.
  • have TB or have been in close contact with someone with TB.
  • have recently received or are scheduled to receive an immunization (vaccine). You should avoid receiving live vaccines during treatment with TREMFYA. Children should be brought up to date with all vaccines before starting TREMFYA
  • are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. It is not known if TREMFYA can harm your unborn baby.
    Pregnancy Registry: If you become pregnant during treatment with TREMFYA, talk to your healthcare provider about registering in the pregnancy exposure registry for TREMFYA. You can enroll by visiting www.mothertobaby.org/ongoing-study/tremfya-guselkumab, by calling 1-877-311-8972, or emailing MotherToBaby@health.ucsd.edu. The purpose of this registry is to collect information about the safety of TREMFYA during pregnancy.
  • are breastfeeding or plan to breastfeed. It is not known if TREMFYA passes into your breast milk.

Tell your healthcare provider about all the medicines you take, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements.

What are the possible side effects of TREMFYA?

TREMFYA may cause serious side effects. See "What is the most important information I should know about TREMFYA?"

The most common side effects of TREMFYA include: respiratory tract infections, headache, injection site reactions, joint pain (arthralgia), diarrhea, stomach flu (gastroenteritis), fungal skin infections, herpes simplex infections, stomach pain, bronchitis, feeling very tired (fatigue), fever (pyrexia), and skin rash.

These are not all the possible side effects of TREMFYA. Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.

Use TREMFYA exactly as your healthcare provider tells you to use it.

Please read the full Prescribing Information, including Medication Guide, for TREMFYA and discuss any questions that you have with your doctor.

You are encouraged to report negative side effects of prescription drugs to the FDA. Visit www.fda.gov/medwatch, or call 1-800-FDA-1088.

Dosage Forms and Strengths: TREMFYA is available as 100 mg/mL and 200 mg/2mL for subcutaneous injection and as a 200 mg/20 mL (10 mg/mL) single dose vial for intravenous infusion.

Global, social-first campaign gives well-known hosts the chance to be guests themselves, with locally inspired creative, new consumer research and bookable experiences

ATLANTA, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- It's time to leave "host mode" at home. New data from IHG Hotels & Resorts finds that two-thirds of travelers who often play the role of host among family and friends say organizing a trip can feel like another job, and they're ready to swap the to-do list for being taken care of.

Enter "When the Host Needs Hosting," IHG's global, social-first campaign rooted in the idea that even the best hosts deserve to be hosted. Across the United States, Mexico, Australia, Japan, the United Kingdom and Germany, the campaign features some of the world's most beloved personalities taking a break from their usual host roles to experience IHG hospitality firsthand, this time as a guest.

"At IHG, we know a lot about what it means to be a great host, and how much thought goes into making someone feel truly welcome," said Connor Smith, Senior Vice President of Global Brands – Luxury, Lifestyle, Masterbrand and Global Creative Director. "With a portfolio of 21 hotel brands spanning over 100 countries around the world, we have the opportunity to create meaningful experiences that make every guest feel genuinely cared for. 'When the Host Needs Hosting' is a reminder that great hospitality is about more than where you stay. It's about how you feel while you're there."

While united by a global theme, each market brings its own perspective to the campaign, drawing on local personalities, cultural insights and new research* to explore what hosting and being hosted means around the world.

United States
Kicking off in the U.S., comedian, media personality and celebrity interviewer, Amelia Dimoldenberg trades her usual role as a host for a well-earned stay offering a playful look at what happens when the person asking all the questions finally gets to switch off. The collaboration also inspired "Hosted Like a Host," a limited-time bookable hotel experience bringing Dimoldenberg's favorite ways to travel, unwind and indulge to select IHG hotels.

Mexico 
In Mexico, television host, model and entrepreneur Montserrat Oliver brings "Viajar a la Mexicana" to life, celebrating the warmth, spontaneity and joyful spirit of Mexican travel and hospitality. Rooted in a culture where making others feel welcome and cared for comes naturally, the campaign gives Oliver a chance to experience that same hospitality herself after more than three decades of hosting.

Australia
Australians spend an estimated 478 million hours each year planning, preparing, hosting and cleaning up after get-togethers, according to new research from IHG and YouGov. In celebration of the country's everyday hosts, IHG partnered with celebrity chef and TV host Melissa Leong to turn the tables on hosting, inviting her to step out of the kitchen and into the guest suite. The campaign continues on-property with five limited-time hotel experiences inspired by Melissa Leong's own hosting style, available for IHG One Rewards members to bid on using points through Nov. 20, 2026 (or later).  

Japan
In Japan, local research offers another perspective on hosting: those who regularly care for others often find joy in doing so, while also valuing opportunities to relax on their own terms. Actor and artist Dean Fujioka brings that insight to life in "When the Host Needs Hosting: Travel, Your Way," exploring two distinct stays through Hotel Indigo's connection to local neighborhoods and Kimpton's personalized approach to hospitality. IHG One Rewards members can also access behind-the-scenes footage and an interview with Fujioka about his personal travel preferences.

U.K.
In the U.K., new research from IHG and OnePoll revealed that nearly six in ten (58%) people who regularly take care of others and organize group plans find themselves carrying those responsibilities with them when they go away. TV presenter Josie Gibson puts that insight at the heart of her hotel stays, handing over the planning and embracing a trip where someone else takes care of the details. IHG One Rewards members can also bid on limited-time experiences inspired by Josie Gibson's favorite ways to travel, unwind and indulge through Dec. 28, 2026 (or later).

Germany 
In Germany, host, actress and DJ Palina Rojinski explores distinctly different ways to unwind across three IHG brands, from yoga at Kimpton to drinks at Ruby Hotels' round-the-clock bar and discovering the neighborhood with Hotel Indigo. Her experiences also inspired limited-time "Hosted Like Palina" stays at select properties across Germany through Dec. 28, 2026 (or later).

Looking to be hosted like a host? In select markets, IHG One Rewards members can use points to bid on select talent-inspired hotel experiences through IHG One Rewards Access. Visit auctions.ihg.com to learn more.

PRINCETON, N.J., Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- CytoSorbents Corporation (NASDAQ: CTSO, the "Company"), a leader in the treatment of life-threatening conditions in the intensive care unit and cardiac surgery using blood purification, today announced a $6.25 million common stock financing.

CytoSorbents Secures $6.25M At-Market Financing, Cuts Debt by $5.25M, and Extends Debt Maturity to 2028

Registered Direct Offering

The Company has entered into securities purchase agreements with certain institutional and accredited investors and certain insiders of the Company for the issuance and sale in a registered direct offering (the "Offering") priced at-the-market under Nasdaq rules of (i) an aggregate of 556,681 shares (the "Common Shares") of the Company's common stock, par value $0.001 per share (the "Common Stock"), at a purchase price of $4.94 per share, and 96,527 shares of Common Stock to the Company's directors and certain executive officers at an offering price of $5.18 per share, which was the consolidated closing bid price of our Common Stock on The Nasdaq Capital Market on November 18, 2026, and (ii) pre-funded warrants (the "Pre-Funded Warrants") to purchase up to an aggregate of 151,822 shares of Common Stock (the "Pre-Funded Warrant Shares," together with the Common Shares, the "Shares"), at a purchase price of $4.939 per Pre-Funded Warrant, equal to the purchase price per Common Share less $0.001. Each Pre-Funded Warrant is immediately exercisable for one share of Common Stock at an exercise price of $0.001 per Pre-Funded Warrant Share until such Pre-Funded Warrants are exercised in full.

The Offering is expected to consist of approximately $4.0 million of gross cash proceeds, with approximately 75% of the Offering subscribed for by existing shareholders and members of the Company's management and Board of Directors.

H.C. Wainwright & Co. is acting as exclusive placement agent for the Offering.  WBB Securities, LLC is acting as financial advisor in connection with the Offering.

The Offering is expected to close on or about November 20, 2026, subject to satisfaction of customary closing conditions. Gross proceeds from the Offering are expected to be approximately $4.0 million, before deducting placement agent fees, financial advisor fees and offering expenses payable by the Company. The Company intends to use the net proceeds for (i) the repayment of $3.0 million of outstanding principal under its existing loan agreement with Avenue Capital Group ("Avenue"), together with a $52,500 prepayment fee and a $270,000 final payment, and (ii) general corporate and working capital purposes.

Avenue Credit Facility Amendment

Concurrently with the Offering, the Company entered into the Third Amendment to Loan Documents (the "Avenue Amendment"), dated November 19, 2026, to its existing Loan and Security Agreement dated June 28, 2024, as amended, with Avenue. 

Key terms include:

  • Debt reduction of $5.25 million:  Repayment of $3.0 million of principal in cash from the Offering proceeds, plus a $52,500 prepayment fee and a $270,000 final payment, and satisfaction of $2.25 million of principal through the issuance of 455,465 shares of Common Stock to Avenue Venture Opportunities Fund, L.P. at the Offering price of $4.94 per share. Following these transactions, $12.25 million of principal will remain outstanding, down from $17.5 million. The Company expects to save approximately $0.7 million in interest expense over 12 months.
  • Maturity extended one year:  The maturity date is extended from July 1, 2027 to July 1, 2028.
  • Interest-only period extended 15 months:  Interest-only payments are extended through March 31, 2028, with a further three-month extension available if the Company has received FDA marketing approval for DrugSorb-ATR by that date, subject to other conditions.
  • New conversion rights:  Avenue's existing $2.0 million conversion right is replaced with the right to convert (i) up to $3.0 million of principal into Common Stock at $6.916 per share, equal to 140% of the $4.94 Offering price, exercisable at any time, and (ii) up to an additional $3.125 million of principal at $8.645 per share, equal to 175% of the Offering price, exercisable beginning on the earlier of FDA marketing approval of DrugSorb-ATR and January 1, 2028. Any conversion would further reduce the Company's outstanding debt.
  • Other terms: The Avenue Amendment also modifies certain beneficial ownership limitations and financial covenants, provides certain registration rights and provides for a back-end fee of $250,000, payable on July 1, 2028 (or earlier repayment) and waived if Avenue achieves a net profit of at least 300% on the initial $2.25 million repayment shares.

Of the shares issued to Avenue in satisfaction of $2.25 million of principal, shares satisfying $1.0 million of principal (the "Registered Shares") will be issued pursuant to the Company's effective shelf registration statement on Form S-3 (File No. 333-281062), and shares satisfying the remaining $1.25 million of principal will be issued in a transaction exempt from registration under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the "Securities Act"). The shares issued to Avenue are in addition to the securities issued in the Offering and will not generate additional cash proceeds to the Company. The cash repayment and issuance of shares to Avenue in satisfaction of the Company's indebtedness are expected to occur substantially concurrently with the closing of the Offering, subject to applicable closing conditions. 

Registration and Offering Information

The Common Shares, Pre-Funded Warrants, Pre-Funded Warrant Shares and Registered Shares are being offered and sold pursuant to a "shelf" registration statement on Form S-3 (File No. 333-281062), which was declared effective by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") on September 30, 2024. The Offering is being made only by means of a prospectus supplement and accompanying prospectus forming part of the effective registration statement. A final prospectus supplement and accompanying prospectus relating to the Offering and the Registered Shares will be filed with the SEC. Electronic copies may be obtained, when available, on the SEC's website at www.sec.gov or by contacting H.C. Wainwright & Co., LLC, 430 Park Avenue, 3rd Floor, New York, New York 10022, at placements@hcwco.com or (212) 856-5711.

The shares issued to Avenue in satisfaction of the remaining $1.25 million of principal are being issued in a transaction not involving a public offering and have not been registered under the Securities Act or applicable state securities laws. Such shares may not be offered or sold in the United States absent registration or an applicable exemption from registration. The Company has agreed to file a registration statement with the SEC covering the resale of these shares.

About CytoSorbents Corporation (NASDAQ: CTSO)

CytoSorbents Corporation is a leader in the treatment of life-threatening conditions in the intensive care unit and cardiac surgery through blood purification. CytoSorbents' proprietary blood purification technologies are based on biocompatible, highly porous polymer beads that can actively remove toxic substances from blood and other bodily fluids by pore capture and surface adsorption. Cartridges filled with these beads can be used with standard blood pumps already in the hospital (e.g. dialysis, continuous renal replacement therapy or CRRT, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation or ECMO, and heart-lung machines), where blood is repeatedly recirculated outside the body, through our cartridges where toxic substances are removed, and then back into the body. CytoSorbents' technologies are used in a number of broad applications. Specifically, two important applications are 1) the removal of blood thinners during and after cardiothoracic surgery to reduce the risk of severe bleeding, and 2) the removal of inflammatory agents and toxins in common critical illnesses that can lead to massive inflammation, organ failure and patient death. The breadth of these critical illnesses includes, for example, sepsis, burn injury, trauma, lung injury, liver failure, cytokine release syndrome, and pancreatitis as well as the removal of liver toxins that accumulate in acute liver dysfunction or failure, and the removal of myoglobin in severe rhabdomyolysis that can otherwise lead to renal failure. In these diseases, the risk of death can be extremely high, and there are few, if any, effective treatments.

CytoSorbents' lead product, CytoSorb®, is approved in the European Union and distributed in over 70 countries worldwide, with more than 300,000 devices used cumulatively to date. CytoSorb was originally launched in the European Union under CE mark as the first cytokine adsorber. Additional CE mark extensions were granted for bilirubin and myoglobin removal in clinical conditions such as liver disease and trauma, respectively, and for ticagrelor and rivaroxaban removal in cardiothoracic surgery procedures. CytoSorb has also received FDA Emergency Use Authorization in the United States for use in adult critically ill COVID-19 patients with impending or confirmed respiratory failure. CytoSorb is not yet approved or cleared in the United States.

In the U.S. and Canada, CytoSorbents is developing the DrugSorb™-ATR antithrombotic removal system, an investigational device based on an equivalent polymer technology to CytoSorb, to reduce the severity of perioperative bleeding in high-risk surgery due to blood thinning drugs. It has received two FDA Breakthrough Device Designations: one for the removal of ticagrelor and another for the removal of the direct oral anticoagulants (DOAC) apixaban and rivaroxaban in a cardiopulmonary bypass circuit during urgent cardiothoracic surgery. The Company is actively pursuing regulatory approval of DrugSorb-ATR with the U.S. FDA and will pursue regulatory approval with Health Canada with better visibility from the FDA. DrugSorb-ATR is not yet granted or approved in either the U.S. or Canada.

The Company has numerous marketed products and products under development based upon this unique blood purification technology protected by many issued U.S. and international patents and registered trademarks, and multiple patent applications pending, including ECOS-300CY®, CytoSorb-XL™, HemoDefend-RBC™, HemoDefend-BGA™, VetResQ®, K+ontrol™, DrugSorb™, ContrastSorb, PuriFi®, HotSwap®, and others. Lee brings more than three decades of experience in financial services, including serving as Chief Risk Officer at Goldman Sachs, where he developed deep expertise in enterprise risk management, financial oversight, regulatory capital, and corporate governance.

Company's 16-Qubit Algorithm Produces Results Advancing the Potential for More Computationally Efficient Nuclear Modeling

TEL AVIV, Israel, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Quantum X Labs (the "Company" or "QXL"), a developer of advanced quantum computing technologies, today announced a technological milestone achieved by its Nuclear Simulation Team, successfully executing a quantum algorithm designed to simulate photon transport through shielding materials on IBM's Fez superconducting quantum processor.

The experiment demonstrated the ability of a 16-qubit quantum algorithm to accurately reproduce key characteristics of photon propagation, scattering, attenuation and detection through a two-dimensional tungsten collimator, producing results closely aligned with analytical calculations and classical simulations.

Beyond demonstrating accuracy, the significance of the experiment lies in the potential of quantum algorithms to reduce the computational resources required for complex nuclear simulations.

Conventional GPU-based Monte Carlo simulations rely on processing large numbers of individual particle histories to calculate radiation behavior, often requiring substantial computational resources. Quantum X Labs is developing an alternative approach that uses quantum-state preparation and reversible quantum operations to encode particle transport probabilities and evaluate detection outcomes.

In the experiment, each measurement point was evaluated using 4,096 quantum shots, with results closely matching classical references. The demonstrated circuit provides a foundation for future quantum amplitude estimation, which could reduce the sampling effort needed to estimate radiation transport probabilities. The experiment did not implement amplitude estimation or establish an efficiency advantage over GPU-based methods.

The experiment simulated the transport of 140 keV photons through a tungsten collimator, evaluating the effects of shielding attenuation, channel geometry and detector energy thresholds.

Following hardware-noise mitigation, the quantum algorithm demonstrated:

  • High accuracy: Root-mean-square deviations of approximately 0.03–0.04 compared with exact classical statevector simulation results.
  • Successful radiation modeling: Accurate reproduction of changes in photon detection probability resulting from variations in tungsten attenuation and channel width.
  • Real quantum hardware validation: Successful execution of the 16-qubit algorithm on IBM's Fez superconducting quantum processor.

"What makes this achievement important is not simply that our quantum algorithm reproduced classical simulation results, but that we demonstrated a coherent and efficient oracle that can serve as a foundation for quantum amplitude estimation," said David Shnaiderov, Head of Nuclear Quantum at Quantum X Labs. "Conventional GPU-based methods can require large numbers of particle histories. Our next objective is to integrate amplitude estimation and test whether it can deliver comparable accuracy with fewer sampling operations. Demonstrating the underlying circuit on real quantum hardware is an important step toward that goal."

Radiation transport simulation plays an important role across the nuclear energy, aerospace, defense, medical imaging and radiation shielding industries. More computationally efficient simulation methods could support increasingly complex system designs while potentially reducing computational requirements.

Quantum X Labs intends to expand the complexity of its nuclear simulation algorithms, integrate quantum amplitude estimation with the demonstrated oracle, and benchmark sampling requirements and computational performance against GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo methods.
